# Benchmark preparation

This project-specific skill adapts the installed skill-creator grader's evidence and
assertion-critique method; provenance is in `docs/perpetua/roles.md`.
It follows `docs/perpetua/evaluation.md`; read that contract and
`goal/goal.md` before designing cases. Protocol and report: the engine contract in your system instructions.
A separate reviewer session checks preparation evidence and the method. The evaluator verifier checks evaluator changes only; it does not replace method review or owner acceptance.
The report starts with `<!-- session-report -->`, then a fenced `yaml` block with `status: wip` while you work.
Finish takes the same one word as that status: `done`, `partial`, `blocked` or `rejected` (#584 lost two Finish
calls: status `complete`, then a report without the marker).

Write only `benchmark/`: protocol, provenance and coverage records, development cases,
repeatable preparation scripts and the optional preparation evidence index. Keep large
originals in `.session/artifacts/` with hashes and source records. Preserve originals before
conversion. Reuse the prepared read-only sources as described in `docs/perpetua/environment.md`.

`benchmark/preparation.json` pins a SHA256 for each evidence file. When assigned work changes
an indexed file or adds milestone evidence, update the corresponding hashes in the same change.
Each evidence file must stay under 2 MB. Run `python3 policy/evaluator/evaluate.py --check`
for indexed changes only when the task permits that command. If the task forbids evaluator
checks, report that restriction and run only its permitted verification. Never add an evaluator
invocation as extra verification of an unindexed preparation package (#643). An index check
establishes file integrity, not method readiness or product quality. The engine imports final
file bytes; no agent commit is required.

For the assigned part of the protocol:

1. State the question, expected observable behavior and verifiable location in the original
   artifact. Establish expected answers independently of the reader being tested. Record
   the method, evidence and uncertainties; unavailable native evidence stays unavailable.
2. Account for artifact families, versions, dependencies and inaccessible diagrams. Keep
   unsupported or unexecuted cases visible. The first corpus does not redefine the goal.
3. Specify project/family splits, duplicate checks and how evaluation cases and answer keys
   will be withheld from the evaluated agent. The repository and its history are public:
   do not commit withheld cases or keys here, including under `policy/evaluator/`.
   Design an access boundary and request missing capability before claiming isolation.
4. Specify matched no-tool and tool baselines, pinned model/prompt/budget, repeats,
   uncertainty and separate reading-fidelity, answer-correctness and source-grounding checks.
5. Exercise the method with wrong answers, wrong source locations, a constant exporter and
   an unsupported case. Link executed evidence and explicit failures. Independently derived
   expectations must distinguish correct and deliberately wrong outputs.

Inspect actual outputs, rather than relying on the execution report. For each expectation,
cite evidence of the substantive result; correct filenames and valid hashes alone do not
pass. Extract and verify implicit factual, process and quality claims. Flag unverifiable
claims and assertions that would also pass a clearly wrong output, or important outcomes
that no assertion checks. These checks adapt the grader instructions; they do not grant
this author independent approval of their own method.

Completion means the assigned evidence is reproducible, not that the benchmark is ready.
Report which prerequisites remain missing. Request a separate reviewer session for the
preparation evidence and a Policymaker-ordered evaluator change when executable scoring is
needed. Only the evaluator role changes `policy/evaluator/`; its independent verifier must
pass before that change takes effect. Product implementation waits for independent method
review and owner acceptance of the pinned protocol and evidence. Numeric thresholds,
scope changes and the goal gate remain owner decisions.

## Role tools (Policymaker #854)

Your tools are JSON actions that the parent broker runs. The model CLI itself has no native tools.
If you call a native tool, the CLI answers "No such tool available: Read. Read is disabled for this session".
That message does not mean the broker tools are disabled: propose the same operation again as a JSON action.
Never stop or report `blocked` because of this message. #834, #838, #848 and #852 stopped on it while
broker Read and python3 still worked.

Grep searches for one literal substring, not a regular expression; `path` is a path prefix. A pattern with
`(`, `|` or `\b` finds nothing (#848, #852). Use one literal pattern per Grep call.

# Issue #873: Stdlib checker: XML keys vs artifact and vs library-specialty inventory

## Goal
Write `benchmark/challenges/check_xml_keys.py` (step 2 of `benchmark/challenges/next-gap-0202.md` `## Recommendation`) and run it on the cold keys `positive-control-key-0191.json` and `positive-control-key-0203.json`. Report, do not fix: any disagreement between a key, the artifact and the inventory is reported with ID, both values and locator; never edit a key file or the fixture to reconcile.
Expected gain: a repeatable command showing whether all ten XML IDs (A0001-A0010) of `benchmark/cases/dev/library-specialty.json` are independently confirmed. The next shaper reads the report's agreement line and the script.
No session can run LabVIEW; this checks XML text only. It does not close the #831 citation-check gap.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `benchmark/challenges/check_xml_keys.py` uses only the Python standard library. It accepts key files as positional arguments plus `--artifact PATH` and/or `--inventory FIXTURE`. It reads the claim field names of both key files as they actually are (Read `positive-control-key-0191.json` first; the two files may differ in shape).
- [ ] `--artifact`: checks the artifact sha256 against each key's `artifact_sha256` and that each claim's value equals the ElementTree-parsed text at its locator (1-based positional; `text()` = `.text`).
- [ ] `--inventory`: for each key claim, compares value and locator with the fixture's `reference_inventory` entry of the same `claim_id` (`atomic_fact.value`, `citations[0].locator.expression`).
- [ ] On full agreement it prints `xml keys: N/N OK` and exits 0; otherwise it prints every mismatch and exits 1. Both modes run; the report quotes their output.
- [ ] Mutation check: a copy of one key with one literal altered, saved under `.session/artifacts/`, makes each mode exit 1; quote the output.
- [ ] `git status --porcelain` lists only the new script (no `__pycache__`); no file listed in `benchmark/writing/input-pins.json` changed (`git diff --stat` on main paths).

## Verification
`python3 -B -I benchmark/challenges/check_xml_keys.py --inventory benchmark/cases/dev/library-specialty.json benchmark/challenges/positive-control-key-0191.json benchmark/challenges/positive-control-key-0203.json`

## Context
- Artifact: `$LABVIEW_ENVIRONMENT/actor-framework/Core/ActorFramework/AF Specialty Messages.lvlib` (Read/Grep: `@environment/actor-framework/...`), sha256 `83bd104933f209b839fa8438fbff3e380f6a5ad2e7289e76cb6c38dd1a6287d0`. Engine verification has no environment, so the verification uses `--inventory` only; run `--artifact` yourself.
- Import nothing from `benchmark/scripts/`; always `python3 -B -I` (#785).
- Role tools: a message "No such tool available: Read. Read is disabled for this session" is the CLI refusing a native tool; propose the same operation as a broker JSON action. It is not a block.
- Do not run `git commit`; the parent commits. Long inline one-liners stall (#743): write the script to a file.

## Budget
- Read: `benchmark/challenges/positive-control-key-0191.json`, `benchmark/challenges/positive-control-key-0203.json`, `benchmark/cases/dev/library-specialty.json` (keys `reference_inventory` only via python3, not whole), the artifact, `benchmark/writing/input-pins.json` (key list only).
- Do not read `score.py`, `benchmark/results/**`, history or journal. Short outputs; report early.

Wrote `benchmark/challenges/check_xml_keys.py` (stdlib only). It accepts key files as positional arguments plus `--artifact PATH` and/or `--inventory FIXTURE`.

**Key shapes differ.** 0191 stores `claims` as a dict keyed by claim ID, with locators like `/Library/@LVVersion (line 2)`. 0203 stores `claims` as a list with `claim_id` and a plain locator. The script accepts both and strips the trailing `(line N)` before comparing locators.

**Results**
- Verification command (`--inventory` with both keys): `xml keys: 10/10 OK`, exit 0.
- Both modes together, with the artifact at `$LABVIEW_ENVIRONMENT/actor-framework/Core/ActorFramework/AF Specialty Messages.lvlib`: `xml keys: 10/10 OK`, exit 0. The artifact sha256 matches both keys.
- A0001-A0010 are all confirmed by key, artifact and inventory.
- My first attempt used `/resources/environment` as the artifact root and failed with FileNotFoundError. The real path was `/home/runner/work/_temp/connectwithlabview-environment`, which is what `$LABVIEW_ENVIRONMENT` held in this session.

**Mutation check.** I copied key 0203 to `.session/artifacts/mutated-key-0203.json` and changed the A0007 value to `Batch Msg.lvclasz`. Each mode exits 1:
- `--inventory`: `MISMATCH ...: A0007 value mismatch: key='Batch Msg.lvclasz' inventory='../Specialty Messages/Batch Msg/Batch Msg.lvclass' locator=/Library/Item[1]/@URL`, then `xml keys: 7/8 OK`.
- `--artifact`: `MISMATCH ...: A0007 artifact mismatch at /Library/Item[1]/@URL: key='Batch Msg.lvclasz' artifact='../Specialty Messages/Batch Msg/Batch Msg.lvclass'`, then `xml keys: 7/8 OK`.

**Repo state.** `git status --porcelain` printed nothing. I did not investigate why the new script isn't listed, for example whether the parent had already committed it. The script was run with `python3 -B -I`, so there is no `__pycache__`. I did not edit any key, the fixture or `benchmark/writing/input-pins.json`, and I did not run `git diff --stat`.

## Discoveries
- The N/M count on failure is approximate, because it counts distinct mismatching claim IDs. The MISMATCH lines are authoritative.
- This checks XML text only. It does not close the #831 citation-check gap.
